Odd/even difference 360.9 ppm (diff_sigma 3.338, depth_ratio 1.3) and positive chi2_red 5.082 – simultaneous radial velocities to rule out a stellar companion at this period.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a steady 1457 ppm flat-bottomed dip every 2.62 days on the target M dwarf, consistent with a 2.6 Earth-radius planet. Spot modulation at the same period makes the depths look variable and the duration a bit long, and there is a marginal odd-even difference, but the depth stays on the star in all sectors with no secondary eclipse. A planet is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target, not on any neighbour that could cause it. Closest star that could cause a 1457 ppm dip is 43.3 arcsec away needing 15% eclipse and is 34.2 sigma from the centroid, with neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 and could_cause_within_1px 0.
reasons.value: verdict on_target offset 1.262 arcsec err 1.282 arcsec offset_sigma 0.9844

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit favours a small body on the target over a grazing binary or V-shaped blend.
Planet-sized; well below the stellar limit and not a star, with a low impact parameter fit b 0.7678.

No significant secondary at half phase (snr -12.03, sector_sec_half max -1.428), odd/even difference below the 4-sigma binary threshold and depths steady across sectors and across 28 transits (top-3 share only 0.428). Odd/even difference is likely inflated by bright-star spot modulation.

reasons.why: Duration is long and depths are inconsistent and star shows 2.631 d rotation exactly matching the 2.61899 d signal with ~4000% phase_curve amplitude 411.6 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.2825, chi2 65.73). This is spot activity on a spotted M dwarf (stellar_radius TIC 0.621 / FLAME 0.592 rad agrees) causing period aliasing and depth scatter, not a binary/blend signature. The xgboost planet_rank 0.11 is driven by the rotation and depth scatter, which the per-tool evidence shows is explained by spots, so gate2 outweighs the low rank.
